effective_resolution_note: edges move in 2 px steps: the render was upsampled ~2x (1280x720 native); pixel quantisation ~2 px

camera.evidence: plain light-grey backdrop with fixed radial vignette (203-224 grey); no texture moves; the bird crosses it

view: bird seen from above / below in a plane facing the camera: head points to image -x (left), wings spread along image y (vertical), tail feathers fan out to the right. Its grey shadow falls on the backdrop up-left of it.

objects.name: bird
objects.appearance: green body, purple/red/orange wing feathers, orange peacock-eye tail feathers, red-tipped beak; the only coloured object
objects.occluded: never; never cut by the image edge
objects.reference_point_recommended: beak_x/beak_y (leftmost mask pixel = beak tip, rigid with the head) for horizontal motion; the rig origin is presumably at the body ~130 px behind the beak (body_est_x = beak_x + 130, rough) - displacements/speeds are the same for any rigidly attached point up to flap-induced head bob (~+/-4 px in y)

motion_summary_px.direction: -x (leftward), essentially horizontal; per-frame beak step grows from ~4 px (frames 2-6) to ~16 px (frames 28-46) to ~25 px (frames 52-71), with slower phases each flap cycle (e.g. frames 15-23)

length_x_beak_to_tail_tip.note: bbox x-extent; colour mask may miss ~10-60 px of the faint grey central tail spike tip

vertical_extent_wingspan_y.note: image-y extent of colour mask = wingspan when wings are spread; at minima the y-extent is set by the folded wings / tail fan (~240-280 px)

objects.name: bird_shadow
objects.appearance: flat dark-grey silhouette of the bird on the backdrop, offset up-left (~-80 px x, ~-100..-200 px y) from the bird, partly hidden behind it
objects.note: only the visible (not covered) part is measured; not a physical object

objects.name: backdrop
objects.appearance: uniform light-grey background, no ground features or markings

events.event: frames 0 and 1 are identical (bird at rest pose / duplicated first frame)
wings fully spread (vertical-extent maxima, flap cycle ~25 frames)
no contact, bounce or direction change; bird still moving left at last frame
